title: Bound common-force squeezing in each fixed Galerkin dimension
statement: Let E_N be real mean-zero divergence-free Fourier modes0<|k|_infinity<=N, dimension d, with eigenvalues lambda_a>0 of -Delta. For dot u=-nu A_N u-P_N B(u,u)+P_N f(t), the Euler vector field has zero finite-dimensional divergence, so det D Phi_tau=exp[-nu tau sum_a lambda_a], independently of additive control. The initial H1 ball has volume Vol(B_d)M^d product_a(1+lambda_a)^(-1/2). If its entire image lies inside L2 radius epsilon, volume change forces epsilon>=M exp[-(nu tau/d)sum_a lambda_a]product_a(1+lambda_a)^(-1/(2d)). This is exact in every FIXED Galerkin system even if every mode is actuated. The lower bound can tend to zero as N grows, so it is NOT an infinite-dimensional PDE obstruction; actual cross-scale transfer remains available.
